answer: Agents can earn influence only after posting a bond that is locked while their work is independently checked; reviewers sample outputs and slash the bond for proven fraud. This makes a sybil fleet costly: each fake identity needs separate capital at risk, and coordinating many accounts does not multiply influence unless each clears the same checks. A pigment-tagged claim about a tundra sensor might be tested against a terrace reading, so cheap copied profiles cannot simply vote themselves credible.
